messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: We've traced the errors to node db-04. It's still taking cluster traffic and I want to start looking at it properly.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Before anything else, that node has to be isolated -- it cannot stay on the cluster network while it's in this state. And do not run diagnostics on it until the node is isolated, or you'll be reading numbers polluted by live traffic.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Understood. I'll also want a backup -- our policy is that we take a backup before any destructive step, no exceptions, and I'd rather not explain that one afterwards.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Agreed, and note the dependency: the database cannot be restarted until the backup has completed. A restart mid-backup leaves us with neither a clean database nor a usable copy.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Fine. Once it's isolated and backed up I expect the restart is what actually clears the fault. Customers are still seeing errors, so I want traffic back as soon as we can.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Two more things and then it's your plan. Restarting the database drops the API with it, so the API has to be failed over before the restart, not after. And traffic stays off until the database is back and serving -- we are not restoring traffic to a database that isn't up.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Got it, so we need to fail over to the standby node, and then restart the primary node once the backup is complete. Also, just to confirm, we'll need to notify the team about the incident and let them know what's happening with the API.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Correct, fail over to the standby and then restart the primary, keeping in mind the API is still returning errors on the standby, so we'll be in a degraded state for a bit. And yes, notification is crucial - we need to let the team know that the issue is isolated to one node, not a broader network problem. We should also check the database logs to see what's causing the errors, in case it gives us a hint about what happened.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: I'll go ahead and send a notification to the incident response team, and also to the relevant teams that will be affected by the API failure. And yeah, it's good that we're considering the logs, maybe there's a pattern or a specific error message that will give us a clue about what went wrong.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Make sure the notification includes the fact that we're considering a restart of the primary node, so the team knows we're actively working on a solution and not just waiting for it to resolve on its own. And great idea on looking for patterns in the logs, that's a good way to troubleshoot the issue without having to rely on the customer's feedback.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: I'll add that to the notification, so we're transparent about the planned restart. And I'll also assign someone to dig into the logs and see if they can find any anomalies or error patterns that might give us a lead on what caused the errors on the primary node.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: I'll start documenting the current state of the system, including the error messages and any other relevant info, so we can easily reference it later. And I'll also check the node's performance monitoring to see if there were any signs of a problem before the errors started, just to see if we can identify any potential cause.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: That's a great idea, having a clear documentation of the current state will definitely help with the recovery plan and post-incident review. I'll also check the DB-04 node's metrics to see if there were any unusual spikes or trends before the errors started, and also reach out to our monitoring team to get a real-time view of the system's current status.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: I'll also notify our DBA team to get a backup of the primary node, just in case we need to restore from it later. And can you also confirm that the secondary node is available and ready to take over, so we can make a smooth transition if needed?

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: I'll confirm with our DBA team that they're aware of the backup process and can get it done ASAP. And yes, I've checked with our DBA colleague and the secondary node is online and ready to go, its replication lag is within acceptable limits, so we can proceed with the plan to redirect traffic to it if needed. I'll also check if the secondary node has all the necessary services and dependencies to take over the primary node's load.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: I'll review the incident plan with you to confirm that we're on track to redirect traffic to the secondary node, and make sure we're aware of any potential issues that might arise, such as API cache expiration or session timeouts.
